retrievalFixReview.proposal: Planner permits four search queries but investigate truncates goal plus planned queries to three.
retrievalFixReview.evidence: researchTurnPlanner.ts validates 1–4 queries and returns up to four (lines 59, 69–76, 90–99); researchCorpusRun.ts combines goal with queries and slices to three (lines 133–142). When goal is distinct, at most two planned queries survive.
retrievalFixReview.implementation: Retain goal plus all unique planned queries up to an explicit bounded total; allocate opening evidence allowance using the actual count and retain per-query traversal traces.

retrievalFixReview.proposal: Shared documentary worker has no facet lexical-query lane.
retrievalFixReview.evidence: documentaryRetrievalWorker.ts receives one query and calls lexicalSearch once (lines 6, 17–19); each worker call performs a single semantic query too (lines 21–23). ResearchCorpusRun calls retrieve separately for retained plan queries (lines 135–142), so the loss is within each query call and is amplified by the three-query cap.
retrievalFixReview.implementation: Pass an explicit list of facet queries through the same scoped worker, run FTS per facet, and fuse by reciprocal rank with lane/query provenance. Preserve one canonical evidence entry across facets; make additional local query embeddings bounded and cancellation aware.

retrievalFixReview.proposal: Expansion can spend its next-round budget around the first anchor before other anchors.
retrievalFixReview.evidence: documentaryRetrievalWorker.ts sets frontier to all chosen anchors (line 45) but pushes neighbors in anchor order into a single next list capped at passagesPerRound (lines 46–55). If the first anchor has enough adjacent chunks, later anchors have no slots. adjacentPassages returns ordinal neighbors (documentaryStore.ts lines 301–306).
retrievalFixReview.implementation: Use round-robin expansion across anchors (one neighbor per anchor per pass) with deterministic ordering; keep a per-anchor quota and evidence-budget checks.

retrievalFixReview.proposal: Expansion deduplicates raw passage IDs rather than canonical evidence content.
retrievalFixReview.evidence: Initial lexical/semantic fusion uses document+text+locator as evidenceKey (documentaryRetrievalWorker.ts lines 24–34), while expansion calls budget.accept(adjacent.id, ...) (lines 49–53). The parent subsequently deduplicates content by work+summary+pageLabel (researchCorpusRun.ts lines 190–196). Duplicate rendition/index IDs can therefore occupy worker slots/tokens before parent drops repeated content.
retrievalFixReview.implementation: Apply one canonical dedup key during initial fusion and neighbor expansion, ideally normalized document identity + exact text + normalized locator/attachment revision; propagate that key into parent acceptance and trace duplicate suppression counts.

diagnosisDirectedPlan: First fix the deterministic planner/query cap and multi-facet lexical lane, retaining strict scope authorization and bounded calls.
Then make expansion fair across anchors and deduplicate by canonical evidence content before accepting budget.

Add offline deterministic fixtures covering four distinct planned queries plus goal, per-facet lexical matching, equal-anchor expansion, and duplicate passages under distinct IDs; assert scope boundaries, candidate order, evidence bytes, and partial flags.
Run static/local contract checks and offline retrieval replay against archived synthetic inputs only; do not infer embedding-model accuracy from synthetic traces.

End-to-end generation validation remains pending. This diagnosis does not authorize or start a DeepSeek run; use a no-provider local/mock generator path and validate actual UI citation/context wiring if available.
limits: Archived traces expose only returned candidate IDs, not all candidate texts/scores, so corpus recall cannot be quantified.
partial and truncated flags are budget/context indicators; they do not prove the needed fact was lost.
The 17 failures include writer, verifier, formatting, availability, and budget problems; retrieval changes alone cannot solve them.
All quoted sources here are archived QA synthetic/public-paper fixtures, not real user data.
